findings.title: assume_role with pool re-enters wrapper from pool worker thread
findings.why_it_matters: With OPTIONS {"pool": ..., "assume_role": ...} no pooled connection can ever be configured, so the first query fails with a pool timeout. psycopg_pool calls configure from its worker threads (AddConnection -> _connect -> self._configure(conn)), and ensure_role builds its SQL with ops.compose_sql(), which calls mogrify(sql, params, self.connection), i.e. the Django DatabaseWrapper's cursor(). That cursor() runs on a non-owner thread while the owner is still waiting inside connect(), so it calls connect() -> pool.getconn() again from the worker (the worker deadlocks until timeout), or else fails validate_thread_sharing. The code comment on _configure_connection says not to touch anything on self except variables, and compose_sql breaks that rule. Building the statement only from the raw psycopg connection keeps configure self-contained.
findings.suggested_fix: In ensure_role, build the SQL without going through the Django wrapper. For example (pool is psycopg3-only, but ensure_role is shared): if is_psycopg3, run `cursor.execute(sql.SQL("SET ROLE {}").format(sql.Literal(role_name)))` using psycopg.sql, or `ClientCursor(connection).mogrify("SET ROLE %s", [role_name])` on the raw connection; for psycopg2 keep `cursor.mogrify(...)` on the raw cursor. Add a pooled assume_role test (tests currently use no_pool_connection() for test_connect_role).
evidence: django/db/backends/postgresql/psycopg_any.py:21 -- with connection.cursor() as cursor:  (Django wrapper cursor -> ensure_connection -> connect -> pool.getconn)
psycopg_pool/pool.py:634-635 -- if self._configure: self._configure(conn)  (inside _connect, run by AddConnection worker tasks)

Offline repro (tmp/corr/role.py): invoking wrapper._configure_connection(fake_raw_conn) from a separate thread with assume_role set re-entered pool.getconn from that thread and failed: 'OperationalError couldn't get a connection after 0.50 sec'

findings.title: Stale alias-keyed pool sends test run to production DB
findings.why_it_matters: If a pool for an alias exists before create_test_db renames NAME to test_<name>, the test run's connection keeps borrowing from that pool, which was built with the production dbname. Migrations, test queries, and TransactionTestCase flushes then hit the production database. One way this happens on every test run: when the 'postgres' database is not reachable, PostgreSQL's _nodb_cursor fallback builds self.__class__({... NAME: prod}, alias=self.alias). With pool enabled this creates _connection_pools['default'] from the prod connection params. base create_test_db then only calls connection.close(), which returns the connection to the pool and leaves the pool in place. Any earlier pooled connect on the alias (code that runs at import time, pg_version) has the same effect. The diff closes the pool on clone and destroy but not on create.
evidence: django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:239 -- self._connection_pools.setdefault(self.alias, pool)  (pool keyed only by alias; kwargs frozen at creation)
django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py (_nodb_cursor fallback) -- conn = self.__class__({**self.settings_dict, "NAME": connection.settings_dict["NAME"]}, alias=self.alias)
django/db/backends/base/creation.py:64-66 -- self.connection.close(); settings.DATABASES[...]["NAME"] = test_database_name; self.connection.settings_dict["NAME"] = test_database_name  (no close_pool)

Offline repro (tmp/corr/stale.py): after fallback-style wrapper created the pool and NAME was renamed, main.get_connection_params dbname=test_prod_db but main.pool is the same pool with kwargs dbname=prod_db

findings.title: Docs say pool ignored on psycopg2; code raises ImproperlyConfigured
findings.why_it_matters: The docs tell users the pool option is silently ignored with psycopg2. A user who shares settings across environments and believes that will instead get ImproperlyConfigured on every connect in a psycopg2 environment. The code raises for psycopg2, and the test named test_connect_pool_setting_ignored_for_psycopg2 asserts that it raises, so the docs (and the test name) contradict the behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Assuming raising is the intended behaviour (it is what the test asserts), change the docs sentence to: "This option requires ``psycopg[pool]`` or :pypi:`psycopg-pool` to be installed and is not supported with ``psycopg2`` (``ImproperlyConfigured`` is raised)." Rename the test to test_connect_pool_setting_not_supported_for_psycopg2.
evidence: django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:291-292 -- if pool_options and not is_psycopg3: raise ImproperlyConfigured("Database pooling requires psycopg >= 3")

findings.title: ensure_role removed and ensure_timezone no longer an init hook
findings.why_it_matters: The diff deletes DatabaseWrapper.ensure_role, and init_connection_state now calls the module-level ensure_timezone/ensure_role helpers instead of the instance methods. Custom backends that subclass the PostgreSQL wrapper and call or override ensure_role/ensure_timezone to customise per-connection setup will get AttributeError or have their override silently skipped, even when pooling is off. The wrapper's ensure_timezone() also now has the side effect of closing the pool. This conflicts with the stated intent of not regressing non-pooled behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep instance-level hooks (e.g. `_configure_timezone(self, connection)` / `_configure_role(self, connection)` methods called from _configure_connection) rather than module functions, and keep the ensure_timezone(self) pool-closing side effect limited to the setting_changed path.
evidence: diff: removed `def ensure_role(self):` method from DatabaseWrapper

residual_risks: No live PostgreSQL server: pool behaviour was checked by reading psycopg_pool internals and by offline mock simulation, not end to end.

close_pool() reads self.pool, which creates a pool if none exists, then does an unguarded `del self._connection_pools[self.alias]`. Concurrent close_pool calls from two threads on the same alias could raise KeyError (only on test/settings-change paths).
testing_gaps: No test combines pool with assume_role. Every role/timezone test uses no_pool_connection(), so the pool configure callback path for SET ROLE has no coverage.
No test checks that the pool is reset or rebuilt when create_test_db renames NAME (including the _nodb_cursor fallback path).
